record.title: Business-logic quirks: follow_up string 'false' coerces to true; mark-sent re-stamps and has no state guard; empty PATCH returns 200 no-op
record.description: Source-verified all three quirks, but REJECTED as a security finding. 7-Question Gate fails Q1/Q4/Q6: every /api/* route requires the shared BOARD_TOKEN (authed(), lines 64-68; enforced lines 346-349, 401 without it), so only the key holder — the board owner — can trigger any of them, on their own board data only. There is no cross-user, privilege-escalation, unauthenticated, or other-user impact; the effect is owner-only data/semantics confusion. Correct home is NOT a security finding and NOT a single bundled security candidate: split into three separate functional bugs for the replica-test bug list (S3/S4). (1) follow_up coercion — functional input-validation bug (S3): validatePatch line 127 does `out.follow_up = !!body.follow_up` with no typeof-boolean check, unlike title/description/column/agent/priority which are strictly validated; the string 'false' (and any non-empty string, 1, {}, []) is truthy and stores true. The same validatePatch is shared by POST create (line 363), so create is affected too; the UI sends a real checkbox boolean so the normal UI path is unaffected. (2) mark-sent re-stamp — functional idempotency/audit bug (S3/S4): lines 414-422 unconditionally set `sent_to_qwenpaw_at = now` and `updated_at = now` with no already-sent check and no done/wont-do guard; re-marking overwrites the original sent timestamp (audit history lost). Note the session value is deterministic (`board-<id8>`, line 417) so only the timestamp changes, and the UI hides the button once sent (line ~307), so the API guard is the missing layer. (3) Empty PATCH — functional validation bug (S4): lines 427-433, `{}` passes validatePatch as `{value:{}}`, then `Object.assign(ticket, {}, {updated_at: now})` bumps updated_at, saves to KV, and returns 200 with no field changed; the same applies to a PATCH containing only unknown fields, which are silently ignored. No live test was run (no board key; do not guess/brute-force it), but live testing would only re-prove these owner-only functional behaviours, not convert them into a security finding.

trace.what: PATCH /api/tickets/:id parses JSON body and calls validatePatch(body)
validatePatch: if (body.follow_up !== undefined) out.follow_up = !!body.follow_up — no typeof boolean check, so string 'false' coerces to true
PATCH handler Object.assign(ticket, v.value, {updated_at: now}) persists the coerced follow_up; with {} it persists nothing but still bumps updated_at and returns 200
POST /api/tickets/:id/mark-sent handler, after authed() gate at lines 346-349
mark-sent unconditionally overwrites ticket.sent_to_qwenpaw_at = now (line 416) and updated_at = now (line 420), with no already-sent or done/wont-do check; only todo->in-progress move at line 419
Auth gate: all /api/* calls return 401 unless authed() (BOARD_TOKEN via X-Board-Key or ?key=, lines 64-68) — establishes owner-only precondition for all three quirks

record.remediation: As three separate functional fixes, not a security fix: (1) In validatePatch, require a JSON boolean — `if (body.follow_up !== undefined) { if (typeof body.follow_up !== 'boolean') return {error: 'follow_up must be a boolean'}; out.follow_up = body.follow_up; }` — this also fixes POST create, which shares validatePatch. (2) In mark-sent, make it idempotent: if `ticket.sent_to_qwenpaw_at` is already set, return the existing record unchanged (200, no re-stamp) or 409; do not overwrite the original timestamp. Refusing from done/wont-do is an optional policy choice, not required for correctness — the core fix is never re-stamping; if terminal-column refusal is adopted, return 409 there too and do not move the column. (3) In PATCH, reject an empty validated patch: `if (Object.keys(v.value).length === 0) return json({error: 'no fields to update'}, 400)` before Object.assign/save — this also covers PATCH with only unknown fields.
record.reason: Fails the 7-Question Gate as a security finding: Q1 — no attacker-usable step-by-step request exists without the owner-held BOARD_TOKEN; Q4 — requires privileged (owner/key-holder) access the attacker cannot realistically get, i.e. 'owner can confuse their own board data'; Q6 — no impact beyond technically possible on own data (no other-user data, ATO, PII, or money). Source code confirms the behaviours, but source confirmation of owner-only semantics does not make them security findings, and obtaining the key for a live test would only re-prove functional bugs. Re-file as three separate functional bugs (S3/S4 replica-test list), split rather than bundled, since each has a different fix and owner.
